entries.title: Establish a repository-backed AstroCrown Product Development Memory
entries.context: Important product discoveries and the reasons behind development choices risk being fragmented across conversations and separate technical subsystems.
entries.decision: Create a structured, version-controlled product-memory hub that preserves product strategy, capabilities, research evidence, decisions, rationale and roadmap state while linking to existing authoritative records.
entries.rationale: A new SI or conversation should recover the important product state from Git without depending on the full conversation history. A clear boundary with existing subsystems prevents duplicate sources of truth.
alternatives: Rely on conversation memory and continuation prompts alone.
Create one large undifferentiated project-history document.
Duplicate the existing audit, verification and technical requirements systems.
consequences: Product ideas can accumulate with explicit status and provenance.
Decisions and their rationale remain reviewable and supersedable.
Register validation becomes a mandatory quality gate.
entries.if_modified: Future work can reuse verified product knowledge and trace implementation choices to their reasons.
entries.if_not_modified: SIs may repeat research, lose the rationale behind decisions, confuse proposals with approvals or create contradictory product plans.

evidence.reference: Owner request dated 2026-11-20 to create and use the Product Development Memory.

verification: All registers pass the deterministic validator.
Invalid records, duplicate IDs/titles, dangling references and cycles are rejected.
The repository README links to the memory and explains authority boundaries.

owner_approval.basis: The owner explicitly approved the proposed repository-backed Product Development Memory and instructed implementation.

entries.notes: This decision approves the memory system, not every product idea entered as a candidate.

entries.title: Require deterministic integrity gates against garbage entries, looping and regression
entries.context: Free-form documentation alone cannot reliably prevent malformed entries, unsupported approvals, duplicate concepts, dangling references or circular dependencies.
entries.decision: Use strict JSON registers, controlled statuses and a standard-library validator with duplicate-key detection, exact field allowlists, unique IDs/titles, reference integrity, evidence and approval gates, DAG cycle checks and negative regression tests in CI.
entries.rationale: These checks are deterministic, low-cost, repeatable and independent of model interpretation. They fail closed on malformed or unsupported records.
alternatives: Rely on an AI reviewer to notice bad entries.
Use permissive free-form JSON and periodic manual cleanup.
Introduce an external database or validation dependency before need is established.
consequences: New records must meet the schema and provenance rules.
Cycles and duplicates are rejected before merge.
A validator defect is itself guarded by regression tests.
entries.if_modified: Bad or structurally unsafe memory entries fail locally and in CI before they are accepted.
entries.if_not_modified: The memory may accumulate garbage, contradictions, duplicate ideas, circular dependencies and silent state promotions.

evidence.reference: Owner request dated 2026-11-20 to ensure the established protocol efficiently prevents garbage entry, looping and regression.

verification: Unit tests demonstrate rejection of malformed, duplicate, dangling, unsupported and cyclic records.
CI executes syntax compilation, the complete test suite and validator.

owner_approval.basis: The owner explicitly required operational verification and prevention of garbage entries, looping and regressions.

entries.notes: The gate is intentionally small and dependency-free; it does not replace substantive human/product review.

entries.title: Prioritise completion of the AstroCrown homepage and Genesis Programme experience
entries.context: The owner identified the public website and Genesis Programme page as urgent deliverables requiring high visual and functional quality.
entries.decision: Keep the homepage and Genesis Programme experience as the immediate product-development priority; do not delay them for speculative future services.
entries.rationale: These are the principal public entry points and the current launch/funding journey. Their accuracy, trustworthiness and usability are prerequisites for broader adoption.
alternatives: Build all proposed platform services before finishing the public website.
Prioritise speculative AI features ahead of the core entry experience.
consequences: Homepage and Genesis work receive the first implementation and verification attention.
Future capabilities are recorded and researched without automatically expanding immediate launch scope.
entries.if_modified: Development attention stays aligned with the owner’s immediate launch priority.
entries.if_not_modified: The team may fragment effort across future concepts while core public pages remain incomplete.

evidence.reference: Owner direction in November 2026 to complete the website and Genesis Programme page quickly and to a very high standard.

verification: The active implementation roadmap keeps the website and Genesis experience at launch-critical priority.
Payment and transaction activation remain subject to separate explicit gates.

owner_approval.basis: Repeated explicit owner instruction in the current project discussions.

entries.notes: This is a prioritisation decision, not a claim that the pages are complete.

entries.title: Build genuine user value, repeat use and shareability into product design
entries.context: The owner directed that attention, public discussion and adoption should be considered during service development rather than as a post-launch marketing exercise.
entries.decision: For every major capability, document the user problem, concrete benefit, reason to return, share/discovery mechanism, privacy implications and measurable adoption criteria.
entries.rationale: Product utility, retention and user-controlled sharing can create organic distribution; these mechanisms should be designed and tested without promising virality or using deceptive growth tactics.
alternatives: Treat marketing and sharing as a separate post-launch activity.
Use artificial urgency, vanity counters or guaranteed-growth claims.
consequences: Shareability and repeat-use mechanisms become part of capability requirements.
Public sharing must remain optional and privacy-conscious.
Adoption is evaluated from observed behaviour, not claims.
entries.if_modified: The team evaluates the full adoption pathway while building each service.
entries.if_not_modified: Services may launch with attractive interfaces but no recurring utility or built-in discovery path.

evidence.reference: Owner direction dated 2026-11-20: consider what will make noise and what should be built into services from the start.

verification: Each capability has non-empty user-benefit, repeat-use and distribution fields.
No public growth, ranking or virality claim is made without evidence.

owner_approval.basis: Owner explicitly required attention and adoption considerations to be designed into development.

entries.notes: This decision does not guarantee viral success or approve any specific referral incentive.

entries.title: AstroCrown owns its official community and governance platform
entries.context: The owner clarified that external social networks may provide optional sharing surfaces but must not host AstroCrown's official communities or replace its own community system.
entries.decision: Develop AstroCrown's own first-party community, specialist-group and governance environment integrated with AstroCrown identity.
entries.rationale: A first-party platform preserves control over member identity, community structure, contribution records and future governance. Third-party networks remain optional distribution channels.
alternatives: Use third-party social networks as the official community host.
Create only external community links without first-party participation.
consequences: Community functionality must use AstroCrown identity and its own policy controls.
Governance elections require approved constitutional rules before activation.
entries.if_modified: Community participation and governance remain within AstroCrown's product and policy boundaries.
entries.if_not_modified: Official community functions would depend on external platforms and fragmented identity.

evidence.reference: Owner clarification recorded 2026-11-19: AstroCrown must build its own official social/community/governance platform.

verification: The product architecture identifies AstroCrown as the authoritative community platform.
External platforms are described only as optional user-controlled sharing surfaces.

owner_approval.basis: Explicit owner product direction recorded in the prior project discussion.

entries.notes: This approves product direction, not the production readiness or merger of the current Community implementation PR.
